lead.description: a least-squares fit of a mean that is not linear in its unknown coefficients

self_checks.title: Exponential versus line
self_checks.prompt: For the points (0, 4), (1, 2) and (2, 1.2), which residual sum of squares is about 0.0188, the exponential fit or the straight line?
self_checks.answer: The exponential fit has residual sum of squares about 0.0188. The straight line has residual sum of squares 0.24.

self_checks.title: Exact exponential
self_checks.prompt: The curve y = β0 exp(−β1 x) passes through (0, 5) and (1, 1). What are β0 and the residual sum of squares?
self_checks.answer: β0 is 5 and the residual sum of squares is 0.

self_checks.title: A quadratic mean
self_checks.prompt: Is the mean β0 + β1 x + β2 x^2 fitted by nonlinear least squares?
self_checks.answer: No. That mean is linear in the coefficients, so the fit is polynomial least squares.

nist_nonlinear_ls2002.title: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, §4.1.4.2: Nonlinear Least Squares Regression

overview_sentence: A [nonlinear regression](articles/nonlinear-regression.qmd) fits a mean that is not linear in its coefficients by least squares.
